records.title: The Workbench is a perpetual handoff
records.decision: A fresh capable agent should reconstruct the current objective, settled decisions, relevant knowledge, achieved work and next action from maintained project owners, without the owner rebuilding the conversation for it.
records.why: Continuity is the product promise; a collection of control files is only its implementation.
records.evidence: No ADR states fresh-agent recovery as the acceptance boundary; 0035/0040 imply it. S-046 Outcome restates it as a spec goal only.

records.title: Complete the assigned outcome autonomously
records.decision: Investigate facts and make supported implementation decisions within assigned work. Do not invent the next task or enlarge the assignment.
records.why: Autonomy was requested inside a real task, with an explicit limit on self-generated work.
records.evidence: ADR-0035 + AGENTS 'Assigned Work And Stances' carry execution autonomy and the no-self-tasking limit verbatim.

records.title: Every imposed step must help delivery
records.decision: A mandatory step must provide immediate delivery value, a checkable decision or artifact, or actual risk reduction. Uncertain-value practices remain optional for review.
records.why: The Foundry repeatedly made procedural completion its own deliverable.
records.evidence: ADR-0034 accepted and canonicalized_in AGENTS.md, BLUEPRINT.md.

records.title: Standalone Workbench before coordination
records.decision: A project Workbench must work by itself. Foundry, schedulers, dashboards, sockets and cross-project coordination are extensions justified by functioning Workbenches.
records.why: The unfinished factory became a prerequisite for the base needed to build it.
records.evidence: Both accepted; AGENTS states no coordination system may be required.

records.title: One canonical Workbench source and release home
records.decision: LLM_Workbench authors and releases the harness. GPT_OS and other deployments adopt it; an embedded private producer is no longer upstream.
records.why: Multiple authoring copies caused drift and confused ownership.
records.evidence: ADR-0026 names LLM_Workbench the sole source and records the rejected producer topology.

records.title: Instruction authority and implemented state are different questions
records.decision: Compare accepted intent with live implementation and name an implementation gap, documentation drift, or unresolved ambiguity. Neither source code nor an ADR automatically wins every disagreement.
records.why: Code-first precedence erased accepted future behavior; prose-first precedence claimed behavior never built.
records.evidence: ADR-0027 splits the two lists and names the three conditions; AGENTS State Resolution carries it.

records.title: Governance planes classify a claim in an operation
records.decision: Classify the claim's use, not the entire file or directory. A spec can contain requirements, status, evidence and history, and can itself be the target of an edit.
records.why: Permanent file classifications created contradictions when repairing controls or appending evidence.
records.evidence: 0025 supersedes the blanket ADR/SPEC-as-Grounding rule explicitly.

records.title: Binding requirements live in their current owners
records.decision: Promote each binding requirement into the appropriate current control or assigned spec. ADRs preserve why, alternatives and supersession; agents must not reconstruct binding rules from historical conversations.
records.why: A decision written only in history remained invisible to ordinary execution.
records.evidence: ADR-0002 + canonicalized_in requirement.

records.title: The Contract is a logical claim set
records.decision: Seven root controls plus the explicitly assigned spec carry the Workbench Contract. Do not add a coequal CONTRACT.md that restates them.
records.why: A new summary file would create a second owner for the same rules.
records.evidence: 0033 rejects a coequal CONTRACT.md by name.

records.title: All planes permit CRUD subject to the operation
records.decision: Create, read, update and delete are available across all planes. Append-only evidence and ADR supersession are artifact conventions, not universal plane prohibitions.
records.why: Absolute plane bans prevented legitimate owner-authorized repair and obscured the actual risk.
records.evidence: ADR-0003 states append-only is an artifact convention, not a plane ban.

records.title: A policy file is not enforcement
records.decision: Machine enforcement requires a running consumer controlling the attempted operation. JSON, a manifest declaration, self-attestation or skill prose cannot establish it alone.
records.why: The factory had rules describing walls without an executing boundary that enforced them.
records.evidence: 0005 requires a running consumer; 0029 registers which consumers enforce.

records.title: Tools handle deterministic structure; agents handle judgment
records.decision: Use deterministic tools for mechanical checks, paths, rendering and validation; use agents for intent, ambiguity, craft and honest evidence interpretation.
records.why: Repeated model calls for mechanical checks cost tokens without improving the check.
records.evidence: ADR-0023 also guards against the over-reading (a missing tool cannot fail ordinary work).

records.title: A check can block only what it evaluates
records.decision: A check may stop a relevant unsafe change; it cannot demand global completeness or the repaired future state as permission to perform the repair.
records.why: Individually plausible checks composed into bootstrap deadlocks.
records.evidence: ADR-0020 forbids the global-green precondition by name.

records.title: Diagnostic effects belong to trusted consumers
records.decision: Register diagnostic code, severity, scope and blocking effect in tool code. Preserve nonblocking attention; no artifact chooses whether its own finding blocks.
records.why: A flat red/green report conflated unsafe manifests with unrelated stale links.
records.evidence: diagnostics.mjs registers code/severity/scope/effect; verified 33 attention findings block nothing.

records.title: Ordinary work does not need a Job Order
records.decision: Human-led work and multi-chat continuation can proceed under their actual authorization without creating a Job Order or completing Flight infrastructure first.
records.why: A coordination record became a gate on the work needed to make coordination usable.
records.evidence: AGENTS: 'no coordination system, order form, flight, scheduler... may be required'.

records.title: A report never authorizes its own repair
records.decision: Review findings are evidence. The reviewer does not acquire permission to modify the audited target, dispatch repairs or publish by producing a report.
records.why: Review and repair were repeatedly conflated.
records.evidence: REPORT_FORMAT: 'A report never repairs its target or grants repair or automated-merge authority.'

records.title: Read-only applies to the named target, not every composed activity
records.decision: A read-only review or navigation skill constrains its target and effects; it must not accidentally prohibit another authorized skill's notepad edits or the audit application's own development.
records.why: Category-wide read-only wording became self-contradictory when the audit room reviewed itself or skills composed.
records.evidence: No upstream rule composes read-only scope with effects; AU-0007 is the only worked example.

records.title: Owner authorization is scoped and cannot be fabricated
records.decision: An owner command authorizes a concrete scope and destination. An agent cannot manufacture owner authorization, and a child operation cannot widen the parent grant.
records.why: A callable skill name and a document's existence are not a permission system.
records.evidence: ADR-0027 covers instruction authority order but not the no-widening-by-child rule.

records.title: Separate Proof, Audit and Owner Command
records.decision: Mechanical proof, independent judgment and explicit owner authorization answer different questions and cannot substitute for one another.
records.why: A passing check was sometimes treated as approval, while approval was treated as proof of delivery.
records.evidence: No ADR separates mechanical proof, independent judgment and owner authorization; 0023/0037 each cover one edge.

records.title: Nearest-root boot with explicit outer safety inheritance
records.decision: Fresh, nested and standalone Workbenches enter through their nearest AGENTS.md. Nested rooms inherit declared outer safety boundaries, then apply the local contract.
records.why: Ambient host and parent-project context broke portability and confused scope.
records.evidence: ADR-0026 names the three boot shapes explicitly.

records.title: No machine-global import of one project's interior
records.decision: Keep a project's memory routing in its own entry bridge. A machine-global instruction file should not force every unrelated project to load a private deployment's internal path.
records.why: A layout move broke a global import and unrelated sessions inherited GPT_OS context.
records.evidence: Nearest-root boot consequence; no machine-global import exists in this repo.

records.title: Stable specs own capability detail; boards project active work
records.decision: Blueprint holds broad direction and the spec catalog; stable specs hold requirements, acceptance, evidence and history; the hot Taskboard displays active work rather than becoming a giant second specification.
records.why: Large boards consumed context and duplicated state that should have one owner.
records.evidence: TASKBOARD.md is a generated hot-specs projection with no separate decision store; verified.

records.title: Size execution slices for a fresh context
records.decision: Break work into bounded executable outcomes, with larger unknowns resolved before dependent implementation. Artifact size and delegation should follow actual complexity.
records.why: Long chats and oversized work packets degraded judgment and made continuation expensive.
records.evidence: tracer-bullet skill ships; no written sizing heuristic. Token/byte thresholds were never owner-accepted.

records.title: Keep completed evidence and link successors
records.decision: Preserve truthful completed spec evidence and supersession links. Future capability changes belong in an active owner or linked successor, rather than rewriting completed history to look current.
records.why: History is needed to understand acceptance, rejection and later changes.
records.evidence: AGENTS forbids rewriting append-only evidence; successor-linking has no stated owner rule.

records.title: Six lowercase support lanes ship as structural slots
records.decision: Ship docs, specs, wiki, sessions, feedback and tools under lowercase workbench, even where a slot is empty.
records.why: Undeclared folders and case differences broke clean-clone and cross-platform behavior.
records.evidence: Six lanes present on disk and declared in manifest schema 2.

records.title: The manifest declares machine-used paths
records.decision: Resolve lanes and collections through one validated manifest reader instead of guessing paths or hardcoding old layouts.
records.why: A moved spec directory silently looked like an empty work queue; renderers could erase valid projections.
records.evidence: manifest.json schema 2 declares six lanes and seven collections; workbench-paths.mjs is the single reader.

records.title: Every project has a local Wiki
records.decision: A reusable Workbench includes its own knowledge base; project memory cannot depend on a central Foundry or a particular recall service.
records.why: Projects without a local brain repeatedly lost context when agents changed.
records.evidence: workbench/wiki/ present with MEMORY.md router and SCHEMA.md.

records.title: Wiki and recall index have different ownership
records.decision: The maintained file Wiki owns project knowledge. Recall databases and search indexes are derived access mechanisms with provenance, not parallel authoritative memory.
records.why: Provider-neutral durable knowledge should survive a database, model or retrieval service change.
records.evidence: SCHEMA knowledge_role already admits 'derived'; no recall-database consumer exists, so only the boundary note is owed.

records.title: Traverse from a context map before broad searching
records.decision: Make ordinary project context reachable through maintained routes, with bounded search available for missing or insufficient routes, debugging and explicit audits.
records.why: Useful files existed but an agent following the official entry route could not reach them.
records.evidence: ADR-0042 accepted 2026-09-06, canonicalized in AGENTS/BLUEPRINT/LEXICON.

records.title: Lexicon is a bounded glossary and route map
records.decision: Keep shared vocabulary concise and linked to its owner; local bounded contexts may add local terms without redefining shared ones. Do not rename LEXICON to CONTEXT or turn it into implementation prose.
records.why: Term collisions and sprawling explanations made the common language harder to use.
records.evidence: LEXICON is a bounded glossary with routing; no rename occurred.

records.title: Cross-context relationships are derived from existing owners
records.decision: The project index and context map route to owners; they do not become another decision store, taskboard or registry of duplicated facts.
records.why: A second master index becomes stale and creates another source-precedence question.
records.evidence: ADR-0042 rejects a second master index by name.

records.title: Use shallow, human-readable knowledge organization
records.decision: Prefer a small router and linked notes usable in Obsidian, avoiding gratuitous numbered folders and index-on-index navigation.
records.why: The owner and agents need to read and traverse the same knowledge without elaborate tooling.
records.evidence: SCHEMA line 80: 'Keep every collection flat; do not add category indexes.'

records.title: Guidebooks are Wiki collections, not a new lane
records.decision: Reusable procedures can live inside the knowledge base. Their writing style or common governance use does not justify a separate root lane.
records.why: Folder taxonomy was being mistaken for authority or plane classification.
records.evidence: ADR-0018 rejects a guidebooks lane by name.

records.title: Design Concepts explain the model and link evidence
records.decision: A Design Concept is a full source-backed explanation of one reusable cross-cutting model, with Evidence and Sources and History; it does not replace the Blueprint, ADR, spec or task state.
records.why: The owner needed the shared mental model, not another short requirements summary.
records.evidence: ADR-0030 requires Evidence and Sources plus History.

records.title: Design Concept creation is owner-directed
records.decision: Agents may suggest a new article; owner authorization creates it. Existing articles may be repaired from direct authoritative proof, otherwise visibly marked stale.
records.why: Automatic article creation risks an unnecessary shadow Wiki; silent inference can corrupt the explanation.
records.evidence: ADR-0030: owner alone authorizes creation; agents mark stale rather than infer.

records.title: Parent knowledge is shared; child knowledge stays local
records.decision: A parent owns concepts its children share; a child owns unique concepts and routes upward for common ones.
records.why: Copying shared explanations into every room creates divergence.
records.evidence: Parent/child ownership stated in ADR-0030.

records.title: Update touched owners during the same work
records.decision: As material state changes, reconcile the owning documentation, requirements, evidence and relevant routes. Do not leave an important accepted fact trapped in a final chat summary.
records.why: Repeated reminders to save and update docs became the owner's coordination work.
records.evidence: AGENTS: 'Documentation is part of done; the implementing agent is its documentation owner' plus the routing table.

records.title: Promotion is per decision, with preserved provenance
records.decision: Identify which individual claims are settled, which remain open, what owner receives each promoted claim and what remains in the working record.
records.why: Whole-notepad promotion silently imported proposals or lost unpromoted branches.
records.evidence: Per-decision promotion is implemented in the personal `promote` skill, which the Workbench bundle does not ship.

records.title: Small independent ADRs preserve the reasons
records.decision: Use separate concise ADRs for decisions that can change independently. Keep context, decision and why; use history for routine changes and avoid an omnibus governance ADR.
records.why: The first large governance record obscured many independent choices and made later correction hard.
records.evidence: 28 small ADRs demonstrate the practice; the threshold rationale is nowhere written, and this triage needed it.

records.title: ADR publication must update binding controls and links
records.decision: An accepted ADR's operative rule must reach its named control, with relevant source and navigation links repaired in that promotion.
records.why: ADRs, controls, skills and templates frequently described different decisions after a partial promotion.
records.evidence: ADR-0002 states the rule; nothing checks that a canonicalized_in target actually carries the rule.

records.title: No extra ADR index was originally selected
records.decision: The September 3 ruling chose self-describing filenames, scan-and-increment numbering and in-file supersession instead of a second hand-maintained ADR index.
records.why: An index could become another driftable gate on whether an ADR exists.
records.evidence: RECONCILED: REGISTER.md is generated by adr.mjs, marked do-not-edit, and stale-register is attention/blocks-none. The 2026-09-03 no-hand-index ruling is intact.

records.title: Names and identities are independent
records.decision: Human names may change while durable references remain resolvable. Identity migration must preserve references instead of confusing a rename with a new entity.
records.why: Repeated Foundry vocabulary and path changes broke recognition across stores.
records.evidence: ADR-0041 preserves references and rejects a second global identity.

records.title: Visible base-62 identifiers are local to type and Workbench
records.decision: Replace the numeric portion of existing visible IDs with base-62; uniqueness is per type and Workbench, with no second global identity. Alphabet and width are not settled.
records.why: A secondary global ID contradicted the owner's correction and overbuilt standalone identity.
records.evidence: S-047 open; ADR-0041 says accepting it migrates nothing.

records.title: Objective continuity crosses providers and sessions
records.decision: A replacement agent should recover the objective and relevant working understanding after compaction, context loss, model change or restart, then verify live state and continue.
records.why: A summary that drops intent forces the owner to rebuild the task and repeat decisions.
records.evidence: Cross-provider resume tooling exists (tools/cross-provider-resume.mjs); the acceptance boundary is unstated.

records.title: New live notepads use versioned JSON
records.decision: Use a shared JSON schema and deterministic update/retrieval tooling, while a shared skill guides what is worth preserving.
records.why: Selective structural retrieval and safe updates need more than unstructured Markdown conventions.
records.evidence: S-046 active, TK-002 ready; ADR-0040 accepted.

records.title: Editable resume state plus append-oriented work history
records.decision: Keep a current resumption view and meaningful work history, including sources, corrections and uncertainty. Retrieve a bounded topic with enough context.
records.why: An ever-growing transcript is expensive; a mutable summary alone loses why state changed.
records.evidence: S-046 Decisions: resume view plus append-oriented record accepted; field names are engineering.

records.title: Capture by survival value, not exhaustive event logging
records.decision: Preserve what a future agent needs to continue the objective, without requiring a detailed record of every action or a notepad for every trivial task.
records.why: Logging ceremony can consume the same context and effort the notepad is meant to save.
records.evidence: ADR-0040: 'JSON is a storage format, not unlimited storage'.

records.title: Raw live notes remain local and non-authoritative
records.decision: A live note records working understanding and Intent; it does not authorize work, prove its own assertions or become a raw Git artifact.
records.why: Committing provisional private material caused leaks, stale resurrection and confusion with accepted truth.
records.evidence: Both accepted; sessions/.gitignore keeps grilling and handoffs untracked.

records.title: Dispose only after reconciliation; preserve unresolved material
records.decision: Delete resolved working notes only after important material reaches durable owners; partial promotion never justifies losing remaining branches or unfinished work.
records.why: Disposable was interpreted as safe to discard before the information had survived elsewhere.
records.evidence: S-046 records P-2 reconcile-before-delete under explicit make-it-so authority.

records.title: A handoff is authored for a particular receiver and purpose
records.decision: Select the relevant working slice, verified facts, exact next action, open decisions and exclusions. Reference existing owners instead of copying the whole transcript.
records.why: Authored transfer reduces rediscovery and preserves meaning that automatic summaries omit.
records.state: Historical skill contract; supporting owner direction
records.evidence: A `handoff` skill exists in the personal home only; no Workbench-side handoff contract.

records.title: Checkpointing and handoff are not session termination
records.decision: A checkpoint preserves resumability; a handoff can be prepared early, refreshed or used for a spin-off while the original session continues.
records.why: Treating either as a mandatory final action makes them arrive after context has degraded and stops useful work unnecessarily.
records.state: Historical skill contract; owner acceptance not established
records.evidence: S-048 Checkpoint Retirement is status=planned and unstarted; ADR-0028 still makes checkpoints the durable target.

records.title: Preserve the entire question inventory and stable IDs
records.decision: Keep original question identities, branches, locked answers and open decisions when merging or resuming grilling. A short current-status list does not replace the complete source.
records.why: Earlier recovery attempts replaced dozens of decisions with a small subset and repeatedly re-asked settled questions.
records.evidence: ADR-0040 requires preserving corrections but not stable question identity across merges.

records.title: One live session record; duplicates must declare supersession
records.decision: Merge related interviews when requested and make the active resume source unambiguous. Retain truthful superseded evidence without letting stale copies silently become the next entrypoint.
records.why: The skill's old diary path repeatedly led agents to an obsolete notepad.
records.evidence: VERIFIED DEFECT: installed personal checkpoint/make-it-so/grilling skills still name `workbench/sessions/grilling diary/`, which does not exist; manifest declares `workbench/sessions/grilling`.

records.title: Cross-host transport is explicit, not incidental Git sync
records.decision: The owner wants continuity across machines. Historical live-note transfer used explicit handoff, while the new JSON ADR leaves transport unselected.
records.why: Local persistence and cross-host recoverability are different guarantees.
records.evidence: ADR-0040 selects JSON and local-only; it selects no transport. Notes are gitignored, so cross-host recovery has no mechanism.

records.title: Durable evidence must survive its stated recovery boundary
records.decision: A local ignored file is not evidence recoverable from a clean clone. A pushed commit is not an installed/runtime result. State exactly what each reference preserves.
records.why: Claims of durability often exceeded the actual file, branch or deployment boundary.
records.evidence: ADR-0028 covers the untracked case; release-vs-installed-vs-running is only in AU-0004 downstream.

records.title: Small reusable primitives and thin entrypoints
records.decision: Build skills as reusable behavioral primitives composed by thin entrypoints and compound flows, rather than restating each child's procedure inside every orchestrator.
records.why: The owner repeatedly sought reusable skills to replace repeated prompting; unreachable children caused silent composition collapse.
records.evidence: 17-skill closed bundle exists; no composition contract is written for it.

records.title: Invocation, composition and authorization are separate axes
records.decision: Owner-facing invocation, a parent skill's ability to reach a child, and authority for the child's effects must be handled separately.
records.why: Gating all primitives broke composition; exposing an owner command let the model appear to authorize itself.
records.evidence: `promote` uses disable-model-invocation:true; the axis distinction is real but undocumented upstream.

records.title: A primitive is agnostic to its first caller
records.decision: Reusable checkpoint, save, navigation and handoff primitives should accept the smallest meaningful scope rather than hardcoding one caller's paths or data shape.
records.why: A checkpoint implementation tied to grilling could not support other work.
records.evidence: `save` is caller-agnostic by design in the personal home; the rule is not stated upstream.

records.title: Compose within existing authorization without repeating approval
records.decision: A child may use the parent's already authorized scope; a genuinely new effect, destination or consequential decision needs its own resolution.
records.why: Repeated approval at every primitive prevents useful composition, while unlimited inherited authority is unsafe.
records.evidence: ADR-0027 gives the authority order but no scope-inheritance stop condition for composed skills.

records.title: Skill callability needs verification at the host boundary
records.decision: Check that invoked children are actually discoverable and callable on supported providers, and demonstrate composition rather than trusting descriptive prose.
records.why: A skill could exist in source but not in discovery, or an orchestrator could paraphrase it instead of invoking it.
records.evidence: tools/test-symlink-invocation.mjs and test-skill-catalog.mjs check presence and discovery roots, not that a parent actually invokes a child.

records.title: Skill metadata must distinguish invocation from mere mention
records.decision: A prose mention may recommend, describe or warn about a skill without calling it; a checker must not treat every name as a required invocation edge.
records.why: The proposed grep-based dependency test would reject legitimate routers and documentation.
records.evidence: The invokes/routes/reads schema was an assistant proposal, never owner-accepted; a grep-based edge test would fail legitimate routers.

records.title: Skill names should avoid accidental everyday triggers
records.decision: Choose discoverable names that compress useful behavior without firing merely because the owner uses an ordinary verb in conversation.
records.why: The historical implement name was reported as overtriggering; later installations still use implement, so retirement was not a permanent settled outcome.
records.evidence: `implement` is still in the required bundle, so the historical retirement was not a settled outcome.

records.title: Delete empty document stubs instead of implying completeness
records.decision: A generated document should omit inapplicable sections rather than leave empty headings that appear complete to a later agent.
records.why: An empty stub can stop retrieval more effectively than an obviously missing section.
records.evidence: Cheap, checkable writing convention; no ADR-level constraint.

records.title: Stances change method without changing authority
records.decision: Builder, Auditor, Reviewer and Reconciler are portable approaches assigned by the SPEC/TASK. Loading a stance does not spawn a worker or transfer permission.
records.why: Permanent role departments and mandatory role-change handoffs added bureaucracy to one agent's task.
records.evidence: Four stance skills present in skills/ and in skillPolicy.required.

records.title: Grilling establishes shared understanding before promotion
records.decision: Research facts before asking; expose the decision tree; ask one consequential question at a time with a recommendation; preserve the answer before continuing.
records.why: The owner wanted to decide architecture without repeatedly supplying discoverable facts or recovering lost answers.
records.evidence: grilling ships in the bundle; AGENTS forbids requiring it for routine decisions.

records.title: Plan unknown work through decision tasks before implementation
records.decision: When architecture is unresolved, make the next bounded outcome an answered decision or experiment, not a fabricated implementation ticket with guessed requirements.
records.why: Large speculative plans made downstream execution look ready before prerequisites were understood.
records.evidence: AGENTS already forbids manufacturing a queue; the positive pattern is unwritten.

records.title: Lifecycle stages remain independently usable skills
records.decision: A guidebook composes separately invokable skills; each skill should work in its declared context without requiring the reader to adopt the entire guidebook as authority.
records.why: The seven-stage workflow could not be exercised when stages existed only as prose or rigid orchestration.
records.evidence: Flight stages live only in the personal skills home; the generic lesson belongs to CAND-E.

records.title: One stable shared discovery home across providers
records.decision: Installed personal skills should remain discoverable outside GPT_OS through a stable shared home, with provider discovery routes pointing to it.
records.why: The skill catalog disappeared or became project-scoped when a Foundry deployment or publisher changed.
records.evidence: VERIFIED: ~/.claude/skills (KaydenClark/skills) holds 68 skills including promote/save/handoff/land; the Workbench bundle is a closed 17 and test-skill-catalog asserts it stays closed.

records.title: Bundle the portable core; install missing skills without overwriting custom ones
records.decision: The Workbench ships its own core skill source. Installation fills missing core skills while preserving existing user-owned skills; an external shared-skills repository is not a required product dependency.
records.why: The earlier external dependency made fresh setup incomplete and the publisher risked destroying customized skills.
records.evidence: skills/ ships the core; normalSetup=presence-only, updates=explicit-only; test-core-skill-installer covers non-overwrite.

records.title: Genesis, adoption and upgrade are different operations
records.decision: Creating a new room, adding the harness to an existing project and updating an installed harness have different input and preservation contracts.
records.why: Treating an existing project like an empty template risks loss or repeated setup.
records.evidence: genesis, adoption and update-harness are three separate skills with different contracts and no ADR stating why.

records.title: Adopt real projects without erasing their history
records.decision: Reconcile an existing project's controls and arbitrary prior content into the Workbench structure with a lossless migration and explicit provenance.
records.why: The harness should augment working projects, not require a blank repository or replace their domain knowledge.
records.evidence: workbench-adoption.mjs migrate implements lossless migration; the invariant has no ADR.

records.title: Managed runtime files have one owner and explicit update receipts
records.decision: Install portable runtime tools in the manifest tools lane with release, commit and per-file hashes. Preserve application tools; updates back up managed files and record rollback.
records.why: Shared ownership and symlinked product dependencies made upgrades unsafe and consumers nonportable.
records.evidence: tools lane with release/commit/per-file hashes; root tools/ stays application-owned. Dogfooded here.

records.title: Preflight every consumed source lane before mutation
records.decision: Check the actual source identity and cleanliness of the manifest, templates, runtime tools and skills consumed by an upgrade before changing a consumer.
records.why: Checking only one lane allowed a valid-looking receipt to accompany files from dirty or mismatched sources.
records.evidence: S-032 upgrade-route-and-source-provenance implements multi-lane preflight; no ADR.

records.title: Release, adopted files and running behavior are separate states
records.decision: Keep released version, actually installed version, reviewed version and running source distinct. Candidate tests are not installed-state reviews.
records.why: Publishing or passing source tests did not establish downstream adoption or deployment.
records.evidence: AU-0004 holds this downstream only; upstream has S-039/S-042 implementing it with no ADR.

records.title: Use the manifest's exact integration branch
records.decision: Resolve the integration destination by exact case from the room's manifest, separately from its default branch; declaration does not itself create that branch.
records.why: Some rooms used Integration, some integration, and some had no usable review destination.
records.evidence: manifest git.integrationBranch = integration; doctor registers both diagnostics.

records.title: Review the immutable integration candidate independently
records.decision: Separate-context review occurs when branches combine at integration. A changed candidate invalidates the verdict; earlier checks need not become independent reviews per ticket.
records.why: Reviewing a nearby SHA or every intermediate change respectively weakens assurance or creates repeated stops.
records.evidence: ADR-0037 accepted; AGENTS Branch Completion carries it.

records.title: Target movement requires review of the resulting candidate
records.decision: If integration changes the candidate's content, test and review the exact result before advancing the destination. Do not reuse a verdict merely because the original feature head was reviewed.
records.why: A clean review of one object does not cover another merge result.
records.evidence: ADR-0037 says a changed candidate needs fresh review but does not name target movement as the trigger.

records.title: Remote recovery is proven by the actual ref and object
records.decision: Verify the intended remote reference contains the exact candidate. Missing tracking metadata or a stale fetch refspec is not proof that work is unpushed.
records.why: The record contains repeated false unsaved-work alarms despite matching remote SHAs.
records.evidence: AGENTS says a tracking upstream is not proof of containment, but no ADR carries the evidence-identity rationale; the /land skill exists only in the personal home.

records.title: Preserve dirty work and recover before cleanup
records.decision: Classify and preserve meaningful uncommitted work before removing obsolete worktrees or old paths. Use recoverable checkpoints and non-force integration without overwriting unrelated owner changes.
records.why: Cleanup and relocation can erase the only remaining copy of unfinished work.
records.evidence: AGENTS Safety preserves unrelated dirty work; recovery-before-cleanup ordering is unstated.

records.title: Public products exclude private instance state
records.decision: Package public-safe source separately from private Wiki content, identities, runtime ledgers, credentials, topology and private derived digests.
records.why: A cleaned product is not a copy of the private deployment's operational data.
records.evidence: Public/private packaging is implied by sole-source but not stated; this repo's templates/ dogfood boundary is the live instance.

records.title: Package mechanically; review publication judgment independently
records.decision: Mechanical archive/clean/package/publish work belongs in deterministic tooling; the judgment that the candidate is fit and public-safe belongs in independent review under actual publication authority.
records.why: A publishing script and an auditor do different jobs; inventing a new role was unnecessary.
records.evidence: Same proof-vs-judgment split as R019, applied to publication.

records.title: Integration delivery does not grant main promotion
records.decision: An authorized landing targets the exact integration destination; main promotion remains the owner's separate boundary unless explicitly authorized for that work.
records.why: Agents repeatedly treated completing a branch as permission to advance a more protected destination.
records.evidence: AGENTS: only the owner merges integration into main; permission layer blocks it.

records.title: Completion must reconcile the owning downstream boundary
records.decision: Report separately what was authored, reviewed, remotely delivered, installed, running, accepted and closed. Closure uses the real available owner and evidence rather than an unimplemented ceremonial receipt.
records.why: Components passed tests while the requested usable result remained undelivered or delivered-but-unclosed.
records.evidence: AGENTS Branch Completion covers merge and containment, not the authored/reviewed/installed/running/accepted ladder.

records.title: Human-readable staged setup rather than an opaque giant wizard
records.decision: Keep setup understandable and inspectable through the guide and small tooling stages so the owner can see what the harness is doing.
records.why: A large generated setup mechanism can conceal assumptions and make repair harder.
records.evidence: Setup is already staged across genesis/adoption skills plus small tools; the preference deserves recording, not enforcing.

records.title: Prove the harness improves work, not just its own score
records.decision: Evaluate actual agent outcomes against meaningful baselines; static template quality, document counts and a green self-test do not demonstrate improved behavior.
records.why: The owner asked for scientific proof of benefit from the beginning, before the later governance expansion.
records.evidence: evals/ (condition-blind grader, held-out task_b), outcomes/ (conditions, mock agents) and S-002 complete all exist with NO ADR governing them.

records.title: Use held-out, condition-blind comparisons
records.decision: Hold task inputs and grading stable, compare with a no-template baseline, isolate trials and use held-out tasks so the harness does not tune itself to its own grading criteria.
records.why: Self-serving evaluators and easy development fixtures can create illusory improvement.
records.evidence: S-002 complete: condition-blind held-out path-safety fixture and grader.

records.title: Judge resulting state and honest incompleteness
records.decision: Grade what the agent actually changed and verified, including scope and truthful incomplete reporting, rather than rewarding a confident final response.
records.why: A system that reports success dishonestly can outperform honest behavior on a naive rubric.
records.evidence: evals/tasks/task_a_scope_honesty grades honest incompleteness; the invariant has no durable owner.

records.title: Inspection, observed use and behavioral tests stay separate
records.decision: Label the three evidence types and never pool them into one health score or average.
records.why: A coherence check and a measured task outcome answer different questions and can conceal each other's regressions.
records.evidence: REPORT_FORMAT warns static checks prove no outcome improvement but does not name the three evidence types.

records.title: Evaluated model and reviewer model are independent fields
records.decision: Record whose behavior is evaluated separately from who reviewed the evidence. A static inspection may have no evaluated model.
records.why: A report written by Claude does not prove Claude operates well under the harness.
records.evidence: VERIFIED GAP: REPORT_FORMAT requires target revision and skill-copy provenance but never requires naming the evaluated model separately from the reporting model.

records.title: One finding can have many observations and occurrences
records.decision: Keep one durable problem identity across reports, with repeated observations and separate affected-project occurrences. Absence from a later report means not retested, not resolved.
records.why: Counting reports inflated problem totals and lost recurrence.
records.evidence: REPORT_FORMAT already scopes finding IDs to the report and requires an explicit shared recurrence key.

records.title: Execution failures are not automatically harness defects
records.decision: Keep unavailable runners, missing evidence, interrupted attempts and incomplete coverage visible as execution/evidence states.
records.why: A failed measurement is not evidence of a failed harness behavior.
records.evidence: REPORT_FORMAT has an Evidence And Limitations section but no named execution/evidence failure states.

records.title: Investigate a finding before repairing it
records.decision: Re-read the claimed mechanism at an identified source revision; distinguish confirmed, unsupported, environmental and deferred findings before proposing or applying a fix.
records.why: Upstream repairs based on unsupported reports can introduce new defects and erase useful dissent.
records.evidence: 'Challenged Or Rejected Findings' section requires exactly this, including retaining dissent.

records.title: Audit Workbench owns independent review history and visualization
records.decision: Use a separate review application to retain results across projects, harness versions and models, with a visual interface and drill-down evidence.
records.why: The owner did not want to read long Markdown report stacks or have every project manage its own improvement program.
records.evidence: Audit_Workbench S-001 harness-review-ledger and S-003 decision-first-website own it.

records.title: Central review storage with a standalone fallback
records.decision: An enrolled project receives an explicit central evidence destination; a standalone Workbench retains local reporting. Central private storage still needs an explicit recovery policy.
records.why: Scattered reports made comparisons difficult, but requiring the central app would break portability.
records.evidence: Audit_Workbench S-005 release-campaigns; upstream keeps the destination-optional wording already in REPORT_FORMAT.

records.title: The reviewer must itself be reviewed independently
records.decision: Audit Workbench is part of the portfolio, with independent review of its consequential outputs and self-review exclusions.
records.why: Its own missing integration destination escaped an audit sweep that excluded the reviewer.
records.evidence: VERIFIED: Audit_Workbench S-008-self-enrolment-and-reviewer-independence already owns this.

records.title: Separate source development, deployment and audit roles across rooms
records.decision: LLM_Workbench develops the template; GPT_OS coordinates deployment in the described workflow; Audit_Workbench consolidates and challenges feedback. Reports flow back upstream without the audit room silently repairing targets.
records.why: The owner explicitly corrected a workflow that treated LLM_Workbench as the deployer and conflated review with mutation.
records.evidence: Three rooms verified present (LLM_Workbench, GPT_OS, Audit_Workbench); ADR-0026 names only source-vs-extension, not the deployer/auditor roles.

records.title: Review each adopted release and preserve longitudinal comparisons
records.decision: Track reviews by actual installed release, project and model, retaining previous observations and making progress or recurrence visible.
records.why: One-time reviews cannot tell whether a release helped or merely changed the report.
records.evidence: Campaign scheduling is Audit S-005; the portable identity half is folded into CAND-D.

records.title: Measure owner coordination work as harness friction
records.decision: Treat repeated owner reminders to save, route, reconcile, resume or finish as observable workflow friction, while separating them from legitimate architectural decisions.
records.why: The harness is supposed to carry the conversation and process so the owner does not become its manual scheduler.
records.evidence: VERIFIED: S-049 is active and its TK-002 measures per-occurrence owner coordination hand-backs.

records.title: Preserve visibility and epistemic states rather than filling gaps
records.decision: Distinguish fresh, stale, unavailable, malformed, inaccessible and user-reported evidence; distinguish a capability being available, eligible, shown, consulted and acted through.
records.why: Declared availability and actual use were repeatedly mistaken for one another.
records.evidence: Diagnostics already model stale/unknown states; the shared evidence vocabulary is unwritten.

records.title: Do not weaken criteria to make self-improvement look successful
records.decision: Retain the baseline and grading standard when judging a change. Improvements require evidence; an easier rubric or a current 100 score does not establish the harness is finished.
records.why: The owner wanted a system capable of detecting regressions and still raising its standards.
records.evidence: AGENTS forbids weakening criteria to raise a score; the baseline-retention rationale has no ADR.

records.title: Feedback repair loops are bounded and independently reviewed
records.decision: A scheduled builder proposes a bounded candidate, an independent reviewer challenges it, and iteration has explicit budget, identity and stop conditions.
records.why: Unbounded self-improvement loops spend tokens, repeat findings and merge unverified changes.
records.evidence: Optional automation; AGENTS already forbids the base from starting one.

records.title: Setup proof precedes the feedback workflow
records.decision: The initial fresh-agent setup check returns in chat; prove entry first, then reporting and continuation. Do not require an artificial report or handoff to establish that setup works.
records.why: The first experiment's outcome was repeatedly replaced by ceremony it was not testing.
records.evidence: ADR-0038 accepted, canonicalized in RUNBOOK/BLUEPRINT/S-027.

records.title: Prefer real useful acceptance work over artificial workflow evidence
records.decision: Exercise the system on genuine small tasks. Do not redo completed work or create fake Job Orders solely to inflate a validation count.
records.why: Synthetic paperwork can prove the workflow's forms without proving useful delivery.
records.evidence: ADR-0038 rejects artificial pilots; the positive rule belongs with the evaluation contract.

records.title: Reuse the existing behavioral evaluation runner before building another
records.decision: Assess the existing harness eval runner for isolated trials and JSONL results before introducing a second runner.
records.why: Duplicated runners would duplicate grading logic and split evidence contracts.
records.evidence: AU-0005 is still 'Proposed' downstream; upstream evals/run.py already exists.

records.title: Report permission fidelity across prose and provider controls
records.decision: A declared writable lane must agree with effective provider permissions and supported relative, home and absolute path forms. S-036 corrected the earlier paired Edit/Write model; the invariant is capability fidelity, not that old permission syntax.
records.why: The contract instructed agents to create records while the installed permission file withheld the operation.
records.evidence: S-034 control-fidelity-report and S-036 both complete; no ADR carries the capability-fidelity invariant.

records.title: One durable writer per shared surface
records.decision: Independent read-only work may proceed in parallel; writes to a repository, spec, registry, installed product or shared file need non-overlapping ownership or serialization.
records.why: Parallel agents can collide even when their chat tasks have different names.
records.evidence: AGENTS has a one-line rule ('one single durable writer for shared spec/Taskboard state') with no rationale or general scope.

records.title: A durable task is distinct from a worker or attempt
records.decision: One Job Order represents a durable task/lane. Different agents and roles can take successive exclusive runs; a failed attempt is not automatically a new task.
records.why: Per-person records lost continuity while shared simultaneous orders blurred write ownership.
records.evidence: Job Order / Claim / Run schemas are Foundry-owned; GO-0021 removed the base requirement.

records.title: Rejection and in-scope repair stay on the same task
records.decision: Preserve rejection history and retry the existing task when its scope and acceptance still hold. New scope creates a new bounded task.
records.why: Creating a fresh order on every rejection hid history and inflated work.
records.evidence: Extension retry semantics; no upstream consumer.

records.title: Captain directs; Steward manages bounded execution
records.decision: Keep an owner-facing coordinator's context focused on direction and exceptions. Dispatch fresh bounded execution contexts rather than making the coordinator carry every implementation step.
records.why: The long-running manager chat became overloaded and stopped serving the owner.
records.evidence: Captain/Steward are extension roles; ADR-0036 already rejects permanent role departments upstream.

records.title: Parallel execution requires satisfied dependencies and disjoint ownership
records.decision: Default to serialized dependent packages; parallelize only when predecessor gates and actual write surfaces permit it.
records.why: Nominally separate tasks still collided through registries, specs, runtime bindings and installed products.
records.evidence: The disjoint-write-surface half is portable; the dependency-gate half is coordinator-owned.

records.title: Keep implementation, review and mutation authority distinct
records.decision: An implementation worker does not accept its own review or land itself by inference; a read-only verifier reports evidence while the authorized owner performs the state-changing transition.
records.why: Role labels alone did not establish independent acceptance or a legitimate close mutation.
records.evidence: ADR-0037 forbids self-review satisfying the gate; CAND-B carries the general separation.

records.title: The seven Flight stages must form a real installed chain
records.decision: Intended contract: Sitrep, Preflight, Launch-flight, In-flight, Landing-check, Land and PostFlight-check are separately invokable stages with compatible handoffs and actual installed consumers. Pin exact SHAs at Preflight, Launch, Landing-check, Land and PostFlight-check, where a specific state is verified or acted on; ordinary Sitrep prose and In-flight internal work do not need an extra boundary-SHA field (AC-2).
records.why: Skill filenames, source tests and a guidebook did not establish an executable end-to-end workflow.
records.evidence: Seven Flight stage skills exist only in the personal home; not a Workbench capability.

records.title: Handoffs preserve context and exact evidence, not authority
records.decision: Transfers identify the candidate, scope, state and evidence, reference their real owners and preserve ordered retry history without copying or enlarging authorization.
records.why: A handoff was sometimes treated as a substitute for the contract or a fresh grant.
records.evidence: Handoff-preserves-context-not-authority is the same rule CAND-A must state.

records.title: Preflight checks facts immediately before sensitive execution
records.decision: Bind preflight to the relevant facts and reread race-sensitive state at launch. Receipt timestamps alone do not establish that its assumptions still hold.
records.why: A formerly green receipt can outlive a moved branch, changed scope or competing claim.
records.evidence: The portable half is 'reread race-sensitive state at the boundary'; Flight receipts stay extension-owned.

records.title: One lifecycle transaction includes one Journal event
records.decision: A private authoritative lifecycle tree records state and exactly one appended Journal event per accepted transition, with the lifecycle engine as the sole mutator.
records.why: Separate state and ledger writes could disagree about whether a transition happened.
records.evidence: Journal/lifecycle engine is extension-only.

records.title: Cooperative compare-and-swap is not hostile-writer enforcement
records.decision: Claim only the serialization and protection actually demonstrated. Cooperative exact-tip CAS does not prove remote deletion, force-update or writer restrictions.
records.why: Security and atomicity claims exceeded observed remote policy.
records.evidence: CAS is extension-only; its honesty lesson is generic but already covered by ADR-0005.

records.title: Multi-repository parents aggregate immutable child results
records.decision: A parent coordinates dependencies and idempotently ingests child terminal identities; it does not claim atomicity across repository refs.
records.why: A portfolio outcome cannot be made transactional merely by putting it under one parent order.
records.evidence: Multi-repository parent aggregation has no upstream consumer.

records.title: Bound automatic repair and distinguish ambiguous results
records.decision: Give a durable repair identity one declared automatic attempt and budget; ambiguous outcomes or protected scope require escalation, with retries distinguishing accepted, conflict and pre-transition failure.
records.why: Blind retries can duplicate effects or consume unbounded effort.
records.evidence: Bounded automatic repair is coordinator policy.

records.title: Versioned lifecycle migration has one live writer
records.decision: Preserve old lifecycle evidence as readable history while moving to one new authoritative writer; do not keep two live mutation systems.
records.why: A compatibility path can become a second conflicting authority.
records.evidence: Lifecycle migration with one live writer; extension-owned, echoes CAND-M.

records.title: Date-only freshness uses the declared local day
records.decision: Interpret date-only records in the workspace's declared timezone; deduplicate equivalent local and remote refs by repository/object identity.
records.why: UTC midnight made same-local-day work look newer and coherent refs look contradictory.
records.evidence: VERIFIED GAP: diagnostics.mjs stale-claim says 'older than one working day' and no tool defines the day boundary or timezone.

records.title: Evidence partition must preserve exact prior bytes and proof boundaries
records.decision: When evidence grows, partition it with exact accounting and provenance while preserving historical bytes; do not merge distinct archive introductions or weaken validators to fit a size cap.
records.why: A spec ceiling and pinned evidence sections made a record unable to accept its own next receipt.
records.evidence: S-036/S-038 hit this in practice; a rollover convention is owed, not an ADR.

records.title: Foundry connects Workbench rooms through optional capabilities
records.decision: A Workbench is a project's operating surface; Foundry connects, monitors and maintains rooms using capability contracts and replaceable modules.
records.why: The owner repeatedly distinguished the useful project harness from the connected factory.
records.evidence: ADR-0015 already names Foundry's capabilities; the architecture detail is history.

records.title: Sockets are capability contracts; modules use declared interfaces
records.decision: A socket is a named capability contract, not a department or implementation. Modules must use its declared entrypoint rather than reach around it.
records.why: Renaming departments as sockets obscured the boundary and self-attestation did not enforce access.
records.evidence: Socket contract; tools/socket-contract.mjs exists but serves Foundry-slice work, not the base.

records.title: Socket-to-module cardinality is asymmetric many-to-many
records.decision: A module may use several sockets; one socket may have several candidate implementations while allowing only the declared active binding pattern.
records.why: The one-row/one-module registry could not express the CIC's intended connections.
records.evidence: Extension data model.

records.title: Blessed means a suitable implementation, not owner authorship
records.decision: A blessed module fits the socket and product expectations; being built by Kayden is neither necessary nor sufficient.
records.why: Authorship had been mistaken for technical compatibility and suitability.
records.evidence: Definition correction worth preserving as lineage.

records.title: Halls are vertical functional boundaries
records.decision: A Hall owns its skills, deterministic workers and lifecycle for one function; cross-Hall work is routed explicitly so agents do not load every department's internals.
records.why: The factory accumulated context and unclear ownership when each component knew the others' procedures.
records.evidence: Hall counts explicitly historical.

records.title: Separate domain core, execution engine and orchestration
records.decision: The deterministic domain core stays independent of the sandbox/worktree engine; orchestration composes both and translates scoped policy into execution.
records.why: Putting all domain behavior inside an external sandbox library would make unrelated project logic depend on its lifecycle.
records.evidence: Domain/engine/orchestration split; no upstream consumer.

records.title: Replace scaffolding only after preserving its rules in the successor
records.decision: Retire temporary standalone guard machinery once the replacement can carry its protections; the rules survive even if the old files do not.
records.why: Keeping two competing guard systems creates drift, while deleting rules because a framework exists removes protection.
records.evidence: Sandcastle is not a current dependency.

records.title: Each Hall builds the deterministic workers it needs
records.decision: A shared boundary provider supplies containment infrastructure; it does not own every department's domain-specific automation.
records.why: The early Orchestration Engine proposal centralized too much and blurred functional ownership.
records.evidence: Correction to the all-Pawns model; history.

records.title: Gatehouse enforces passage but does not grant authority
records.decision: Gatehouse builds and evaluates enforcement boundaries and passage receipts; actual authorization and lifecycle mutation retain their named owners.
records.why: The same metaphor was incorrectly used for policy, authorization, auditing and execution.
records.evidence: Gatehouse separation; GO-0006 downstream.

records.title: Scheduling, orchestration, validation and audit have separate responsibilities
records.decision: Timing infrastructure, dispatch/dependency flow, task authority validation and independent quality judgment are separate concerns; monitoring reports on them rather than becoming their owner.
records.why: The thirteen-Hall redesign repeatedly corrected one component absorbing another's responsibility.
records.evidence: Thirteen-Hall responsibility map; explicitly not thirteen services.

records.title: Public source, installed module and running service have distinct owners
records.decision: A module has a producer checkout and a shipped/installed product with an exact receipt; updating the producer is not updating the running module.
records.why: Duplicate paths and stale installed copies obscured what the owner was actually using.
records.evidence: Producer/installed/running split — the generic half is CAND-H.

records.title: Operating identity is independent of the model engine
records.decision: Durable continuity belongs to the host/factory's stores and identity; the current model is replaceable and an agent/run is disposable.
records.why: The old fixed host-plus-model roster rejected cloud instances and made a model change look like a different being.
records.evidence: Provider-neutral identity; the generic half is already in ADR-0041 and CAND-D.

records.title: CAS separates owner-facing direction, factory execution and outside-world assistance
records.decision: Captain, Steward and Attendant describe different scopes of assistance; the owner wanted a personable interface without one context doing all implementation.
records.why: The owner wanted a conversational assistant backed by a factory, not merely an autonomous coding queue.
records.evidence: CAS roles; name collision noted in source.

records.title: A connected system must still cold-start from its own records
records.decision: A fresh agent must find controls, Wiki, skills, current work and verified capability from the deployed system without inheriting the builder's chat memory.
records.why: A system known only to its author is not operational for a new agent.
records.evidence: Cold-start-from-own-records is the same acceptance boundary CAND-A states.

records.title: Cross-machine sync targets selected structure and knowledge
records.decision: Synchronize the intended harness structure and Wiki across hosts while respecting project-specific repositories and private/runtime boundaries.
records.why: The owner wanted reliable PC/Mac continuity, not indiscriminate mirroring of every local project.
records.evidence: Same unresolved transport question as R054, stated as cross-machine sync scope.

records.title: Schematic explains intended design; CIC mirrors live state
records.decision: Keep the explanatory system model and deterministic non-executing simulation separate from the private operational dashboard.
records.why: A future-design rendering was repeatedly mistaken for proof that the real factory was deployed.
records.evidence: Schematic/CIC separation; extension products.

records.title: Show workflow, governance and structure as distinct views
records.decision: Use coordinated views to explain the same system from different questions, including a traceable workflow and governance passage, with inspectable elements.
records.why: One overloaded diagram could not convey both the architecture and how a request moves through it.
records.evidence: View architecture; not a base requirement.

records.title: The simulator is deterministic and can expose failure paths
records.decision: Provide run, pause, step, replay and controlled failure injection in the design simulator, without executing real production operations.
records.why: A static happy-path diagram could not demonstrate the intended recovery and gating model.
records.evidence: Simulator determinism; extension product.

records.title: Draft, explicit send and authorized work are separate states
records.decision: Typed or externally dictated input remains a draft until explicit Send creates durable Intent; an Entrance or dashboard action does not itself authorize arbitrary downstream mutation.
records.why: Voice and convenience controls must not silently send, approve or execute an unfinished request.
records.evidence: Draft/send/authorize boundary — generic value noted, no upstream interface exists.

records.title: Show the selected route and preserve the task's home
records.decision: Expose provider/engine and effort selection, including Auto's resolved route. Changing model preserves the task's Factory home unless the owner explicitly redirects it.
records.why: Model selection and task placement were being coupled invisibly.
records.evidence: Multi-provider Entrance; no upstream consumer.

records.title: A dashboard state change can express intent without completing work
records.decision: Moving a card or selecting an operation requests a transition; actual execution and verification determine the resulting status.
records.why: A UI gesture can make a board say Done while the underlying task remains unfinished.
records.evidence: Intent-vs-observed-state on a board; upstream TASKBOARD is generated, so it cannot express intent.

records.title: Liveness, load, reasoning effort and work status are separate signals
records.decision: Distinguish alive/asleep/down, active worker load, average/peak reasoning effort and queued/blocked/failed/verified status. Do not infer one from another.
records.why: Brightness, model tier and activity were repeatedly conflated; an asleep but healthy system must not appear down.
records.evidence: Liveness/load/effort/status separation; extension telemetry.

records.title: Heartbeat is an authoritative snapshot plus observer acknowledgement
records.decision: Foundry emits sequence, time, cadence, load, workers and effort; CIC acknowledges observer health. The recorded cadence is 60/15/5/1 seconds for L0/L1/L2/L3, with one missed expected beat marking liveness failure.
records.why: The monitor needs an explicit exchange and failure rule rather than inferring health from an animation.
records.evidence: Heartbeat cadences explicitly not generalizable.

records.title: No silent activation
records.decision: Announce activation before or as it happens; an observed unannounced activation is anomalous. Later Lighthouse delivery explicitly excluded Announced Activation implementation.
records.why: The owner wanted to see cost-bearing work begin and detect unexpected activity.
records.state: Accepted historical decision; later delivery deferred
records.evidence: No-silent-activation: accepted intent, delivery deferred; keep both facts.

records.title: Projection is a shared cached entry surface, with visible staleness
records.decision: Deterministic boundary captures can help both humans and fresh agents orient. Every reader sees source and capture age; a projection can route but cannot authorize work.
records.why: Repeated cold-start discovery was expensive, and uncaptured lanes disappeared from dashboards.
records.evidence: TASKBOARD is a generated projection; render-drift is a registered selection-blocking code. Projection cannot authorize.

records.title: Flight Rack aggregates counts and preserves individual history
records.decision: Show active counts at the seven positions and let an individual run retain unreached, current, passed, blocked, failed and repaired history rather than blending all runs into one ambiguous gradient.
records.why: Aggregate activity and a single flight's outcome tell different stories.
records.evidence: Flight Rack visual data model.

records.title: Accessibility is part of operational telemetry
records.decision: Use labels, timestamps and static brightness alongside color and motion so state remains interpretable under reduced motion and in a still image.
records.why: A moving or colored light alone cannot reliably communicate liveness or risk.
records.evidence: Accessibility in telemetry; retain for any future interface.

records.title: Owner-visible acceptance goes beyond server health
records.decision: Verify exact installed/runtime provenance and then exercise the authenticated desktop/mobile interface. A listening service or successful health response is not proof the owner's workflow works.
records.why: The record showed HTTP success while the owner reported the application unusable.
records.evidence: Owner-visible acceptance beyond server health is the outcome-acceptance rule CAND-C states.

records.title: Python is the owner's stated preferred runtime language
records.decision: The owner said they wanted Python and had not corrected the JavaScript/Node implementation. The conversation asked whether migration was worthwhile; it did not authorize a rewrite.
records.why: An agent-chosen implementation language had become architecture without the owner's intended preference being resolved.
records.evidence: VERIFIED: all runtime tooling is Node .mjs; only evals/run.py, score.py and two test files are Python. Owner preference never resolved.

records.title: Native provider adapters and hard hooks need an explicit choice
records.decision: The owner wants reliable behavior across provider products and liked a middle ground between prose-only rules and rebuilding everything. Particular hook, metadata and adapter schemas were proposals.
records.why: Identical instructions do not imply identical host capabilities or enforcement.
records.evidence: ADR-0005 requires a running consumer but selects no provider-native enforcement; skillPolicy.discovery is the only provider-aware field.

records.title: Parallel specialist ensembles were explored, not made universal
records.decision: The owner proposed a user-facing executive with constructive, critical and engineering specialists and cheaper reviewers to improve quality and cost.
records.why: Different perspectives may catch weaknesses while protecting expensive context.
records.evidence: ADR-0036's four stances deliberately replace agent departments; AGENTS states loading a stance never spawns an agent.

records.title: Track total delegated token/cost burden
records.decision: Evaluate the cost of the whole worker tree, not just the parent context or a single agent's token count.
records.why: Fan-out hides orchestration overhead and can make apparent context savings expensive.
records.evidence: No delegated-cost measurement exists; no cap was ever settled.

records.title: Review stale projects before archiving
records.decision: After prolonged inactivity, inspect save state, remotes and worktrees and present readiness for archive to the owner rather than silently archiving.
records.why: The owner wanted portfolio hygiene without losing unfinished work.
records.evidence: Portfolio hygiene is not a single-room concern; the two-week threshold was conversational.

records.title: Governance policy as data with a derived matrix
records.decision: Keep one policy owner and derive explanatory views; extend the existing clearance policy where relevant. The full matrix, missing-entry behavior and global catalog semantics were not all settled.
records.why: Duplicate tables and prose-only enforcement would create contradictory policy sources.
records.evidence: GO-0004/GO-0006 clearance policy; no upstream consumer.

records.title: Governance verbs name operations; the complete verb catalog remained open
records.decision: Operation names should identify what is done and its context, without pretending every verb is an automatic plane transition. Several proposed verbs and CRUD policy details remained open.
records.why: Naming a verb risked silently granting behavior or inventing transition machinery.
records.evidence: GO-0007 verb catalog left open downstream.

records.title: Job Orders link their sources and bound authority by intersection
records.decision: An in-force order links authority/evidence owners and lists its operations; its authority is bounded by its actual sources. The global-versus-per-order operation catalog was left open.
records.why: Copied rules drift and a task packet cannot authorize a future mechanism merely by naming it.
records.evidence: GO-0021 already removed the ordinary-work requirement; upstream ADR-0015 keeps it out of the base.

records.title: Do not import unresolved Flightbook, Issues or sandbox choices
records.decision: Flightbook assembly details, GitHub Issues adapters, some sandbox integration choices and automatic repair routing retained open or deferred status in their own records.
records.why: Assistant recommendations and temporary bootstrap proposals were repeatedly mistaken for locked architecture.
records.evidence: Explicitly unresolved in their own records; importing them would manufacture decisions.

records.title: Retired producer topology and permanent role cages are history
records.decision: Earlier GPT_OS/Forge-as-sole-producer, fixed host/model seats, mandatory department roles and universal lifecycle requirements were later narrowed or replaced.
records.why: Blindly collecting old decisions as simultaneous current requirements would recreate the contradictions the owner corrected.
records.evidence: Retained as dated lineage inside CAND-R; never revived as binding.

records.title: Plane passage is selective, not a universal six-stop workflow
records.decision: Work may visit only the governance roles relevant to the operation, branch into related records, or change the role a claim plays. It need not traverse every plane before it can proceed.
records.why: The owner explicitly rejected converting a model for reasoning about work into a mandatory linear workflow.
records.evidence: AGENTS: planes classify 'claims and their use in one operation, never whole files'. No six-stop workflow exists.

records.title: Resolve contradictions openly before rewriting the owning claim
records.decision: A correction must adjudicate conflicting accepted statements using the owner's ruling and verified context; relocating or summarizing the text does not settle a disagreement.
records.why: A document move or tidy synthesis can erase the decision that actually needed resolution.
records.evidence: AGENTS State Resolution: 'name the condition instead of picking a winner'.

records.title: Promote is a decision-only operation; save is agnostic
records.decision: The owner selected a separate owner-fired promote entrypoint that promotes only locked decisions, records where they landed and calls save. Save does not know about grilling or end it; the chosen promote exit behavior and related skill changes were deferred.
records.why: Make-it-so, grilling, checkpoint and save were mutually coupled, so saving could unexpectedly end the interview or begin a build.
records.evidence: VERIFIED: ~/.claude/skills/promote implements exactly the GP-22/23/62 contract (owner-fired, decision-only, calls save, save stays grilling-agnostic) while S-048 upstream calls save 'unimplemented'.

records.title: Use repeatable process, not identical generated wording
records.decision: Skill and workflow reliability means equivalent inputs follow a predictable process and produce the same result class, while preserving task-specific outputs and identities.
records.why: Demanding identical prose misses the useful form of determinism in agent work.
records.evidence: Useful evaluation distinction; nothing upstream states it.

records.title: Operational knowledge is part of docs maintenance
records.decision: When the owner asks to update the docs, relevant durable project understanding belongs in the Wiki as well as the touched controls/specs, without copying task state everywhere.
records.why: Agents treated documentation as control-file edits and left the project's accumulated understanding behind.
records.evidence: The ownership table routes durable knowledge to workbench/wiki/ with 'never copied task state'.

records.title: An Example Workbench is a conformance reference, not unexplained imitation
records.decision: Use a pinned example and matching template revision when reviewing adopted rooms; preserve evidence-backed project differences and report unexplained deviations.
records.why: Comparisons without a known reference confused template defects with deliberate project adaptations.
records.evidence: Example_Workbench verified present; Audit S-009 does v3.1.2 conformance. The reference/deviation semantics have no upstream owner.

records.title: Declared support needs a real consumer and fresh-clone proof
records.decision: A feature must be discoverable and usable by a fresh agent from its supported installation; source files and fixture tests alone do not establish installed capability.
records.why: Skills and lifecycle functions repeatedly had no working non-test caller or installed discovery route.
records.evidence: ADR-0038 requires fresh-agent setup proof; the general 'declared support needs a real consumer' rule is unstated.

records.title: A connected Foundry can span multiple factories and one shared service layer
records.decision: The owner confirmed one Foundry with multiple host factories and shared CIC, recall and messaging backends, rather than a fixed host/model seat roster.
records.why: Multi-machine continuity and monitoring should not duplicate the whole service identity on every model switch.
records.evidence: Connected-Foundry ruling; extension topology.

records.title: Owner interfaces should show the next actionable issue and its evidence
records.decision: Show progress, regressions, blockers, freshness and source drill-down so the owner can decide what needs attention without reading a report archive.
records.why: The owner wanted an operational understanding of the system rather than long Markdown summaries as the default UI.
records.evidence: Audit_Workbench S-003 decision-first-website owns the owner-facing surface.

records.title: Unavailable baseline is a third state with evidence
records.decision: The owner selected record-and-proceed for a harness-only migration whose unrelated baseline is unavailable, using the declared reasons and evidence. A failing baseline remains failing; unavailable cannot relabel red as green.
records.why: Host restrictions or pre-existing product conditions otherwise made rooms permanently unmigratable for problems the harness change could not fix.
records.evidence: S-041 is complete and records an explicit owner choice (record-and-proceed) with no ADR carrying it.

records.title: Template customization must preserve fixed control wording
records.decision: A placeholder fill preserves the surrounding rule. Changed or dropped authority, privacy and verification wording must be exposed and restored or explicitly recorded as a decision.
records.why: A Forbidden-to-Allowed reversal was misreported as an expected placeholder fill.
records.evidence: S-034 produces the fidelity report; the Forbidden-to-Allowed reversal is the motivating failure.

records.title: Installed skills carry their own generation and content identity
records.decision: Identify an installed skill by its source release, commit and content hash; an unmarked copy has unknown provenance, not implicit identity with the current source.
records.why: Feedback blamed a new release for stale installed skill text from an older generation.
records.evidence: S-031 installed-skill-generation complete; doctor emits 33 skill-generation-unknown findings right now on this very room.

records.title: Historical adoption provenance is distinct from current component provenance
records.decision: Keep the room's original adoption source historical while receipts and markers identify the current installed tools and skills. Reject unknown or contradictory source identity before mutation.
records.why: Rewriting history to the latest release made it impossible to tell what was adopted and what was subsequently updated.
